declarations.description:
Renders markdown as sanitized HTML in the light DOM (no shadow root), so it inherits styles.

- The markdown comes from the markdown property, or from a child script tag with type="text/markdown", 
which is reread whenever its text changes. 
- Uses marked and DOMPurify packages, for parsing and sanitization. Behavior can be customized via markedOptions property.
- Headings get GitHub-style ids (via marked-gfm-heading-id), with headingIdPrefix in front, e.g. '## Slots' gets id="md-slots".
The prefix stops DOMPurify from removing ids that match DOM properties, such as 'children' or 'title'.
Relative links with a #hash get the same prefix added, so `[Slots](#slots)` and `[Slots](other.md#slots)` still point at the heading.
declarations.name: CorkMarkdown

Takes the same object as marked.use(), including renderer methods. See https://marked.js.org/using_advanced. Or an array of them, applied in order, e.g. to add an extension such as marked-highlight alongside your own options. Property only.

declarations.description:
The primary site header component that accepts various slotted header components and controls their visibility in the nav tray.

By default, background images are set via global CSS properties. Without the image-url or background-image-url attributes, the header will have no background art.

The image-url and font-url attributes are conveniences for apps without a js entry point to make those calls from.
They act on the whole document, not just the header, so use one or the other, not both.

The header also sets --page-width on the document with a {@link PageWidthController }, for layout classes such as l-full-width.
Set the no-page-width attribute to turn this off.

The header bar (UC Davis logo, inline menu and tray toggles) is sticky: it stays fixed to the top of the screen, and shrinks once the page scrolls.
The branding bar scrolls away as usual. The header sets scroll-padding-top on the page (to --sticky-header-scroll-offset), so #hash links land below the bar.
Set the no-sticky attribute to turn this off.

In an SPA using

declarations.description:
A pager for navigating through pages of results. Contains:
- A previous button
- A window of page numbers centered on the current page. Window size is determined by element attributes.
- A next button

Items are links if the pager is configured to make an href, or else buttons that fire cork-pager-item-click.

Colors follow campus's --forced-contrast custom property, so the pager adapts on dark backgrounds where appropriate classes are applied, such as 'layout-section--force-contrast'.
declarations.name: CorkPager

slots.description: Not an actual slot. An optional script tag with type="text/link-function", holding a link function expression (see linkFunction). Overrides the link attributes. It's read with new Function, so it needs a Content Security Policy that allows unsafe-eval (or no CSP); otherwise, use linkFunction. Reread when its text changes. See example below.

members.name: getLink
members.description:
Gets the link for a page. Uses the first of these that's set:

1. The linkFunction property.
2. A link function in a child script tag with type="text/link-function".
3. basePath, useHash and pageParam. The page goes at the end of the path, e.g. '/search/2', or '#/search/2' with useHash,
plus '?' and queryParams, if set. With pageParam, the page goes in that query parameter instead, after queryParams,
e.g. '/search?q=cats&page=2'. With pageParam and no basePath, the link is only a query string, e.g. '?page=2', which keeps the current path.

With none of them, pages have no link.

members.description: For link construction. Path that page links start with, e.g. '/search' makes '/search/2'. Used when neither linkFunction nor the script tag is set. Combines with useHash, queryParams and pageParam, e.g. '#/search/2', '/search/2?q=cats', or '/search?q=cats&page=2'. Attribute: base-path.

members.name: selected
members.description: The child to show. A whole number (e.g. '0') is a child index. Anything else is matched against each child's propForSelected property, if set, or else its attrForSelected attribute. Attribute: selected.

members.name: attrForSelected
members.description: Attribute of the children that selected value is matched against. Default (and when empty): 'id'. Attribute: attr-for-selected.

members.name: propForSelected
members.description: Property of the children that selected value is matched against, with strict equality. Takes precedence over attrForSelected when set. Default: ''. Attribute: prop-for-selected.

members.name: selectedAttribute
members.description: An attribute to add to the selected child, and remove from the rest. Optional. Attribute: selected-attribute.

members.name: fallbackSelection
members.description: The child to show when selected matches nothing, e.g. a not-found page. Matched like selected. Attribute: fallback-selection.

declarations.description:
A simple search form with optional facet buttons. Can be added as a child of the {@link cork-header } element, or of a {@link cork-search-tray }.

On submit:

- With formAction set, the form submits natively. Otherwise it fires a cork-search event for the app to handle.
- The search button submits as submitParam=Submit, and a facet button as its name=value, so the request says which one was used.
- After a search, it asks a parent cork-header to close its nav tray, unless keepTrayOpen is set.
declarations.name: CorkSearchForm

slots.description: Facet buttons: button elements, direct children only. Not an actual slot, but rather parsed and rendered into the shadow DOM as submit buttons. - name: required. Its key in the request. - value: defaults to its text. - aria-label: copied over.

members.name: onNavTrayHide
members.description: Called by cork-header (directly, or through cork-search-tray) when its nav tray hides this element. Clears the input.
